title: Post-incident plan: reservation guardrails, eviction controller, and graceful throttling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a high-traffic window on 2026-02-14 three dedicated clusters experienced cascading eviction storms that caused elevated latency and several customer-visible throttled requests. Root cause analysis indicates a combination of (1) overly tight reservation sizing heuristics that allowed near-zero guardbands for aggressive jobs, (2) eviction controller logic that performed immediate aggressive preemption without a graceful drain/backoff policy, and (3) burst policy configuration that did not isolate per-customer burst budgets, enabling noisy neighbors to consume shared burst capacity.

Objective: Implement a set of guardrails and controller changes so that dedicated clusters: (a) maintain a minimum safety reservation (guardband) to avoid reactive mass-evictions, (b) apply a soft-eviction path that prefers throttling and graceful draining over immediate preemption for lower-priority workloads, and (c) split burst buckets and introduce per-customer burst smoothing to reduce noisy-neighbor impact. Add telemetry and canary rollout plan to validate in production without causing regressions.

Scope and out-of-scope: This ticket covers the serving/runtime controller changes, scheduling heuristics, and runtime config defaults. It includes API knobs for Dedicated capacity admins to tune guardbands and burst policies. It does NOT cover UI changes in Console (separate PM ticket) or long-term economic analysis of reservation pricing (finance scope).
acceptance_criteria: Default reservation guardband introduced and documented (config default = 15% of capacity, adjustable per-namespace).
Eviction controller implements a two-stage flow: soft-throttle (grace window) -> prioritized graceful drain -> hard-evict with exponential backoff; unit and integration tests added.
Burst policy updated to use per-customer token buckets with smoothing window; noisy-customer isolation validated via synthetic replay harness.
Canary rollout plan executed across 3 clusters with SLO telemetry showing no regression in p95 latency and no more than 2% increase in cost for dedicated customers during test window.
Operational runbook updated and on-call alerts added (new alert: cluster-reservation-saturation >= 90% for > 10m).

Proposal: introduce configurable guardband percent and shift default to 15% while we monitor. See spike notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/spikes/reservation-heuristic-2026-02-17
